In [[mathematics]], a '''continuous module''' is a [[module (mathematics)|module]] ''M'' such that every [[submodule]] of ''M'' is [[essential submodule|essential]] in a [[direct sum of modules|direct sum]]mand and every submodule of ''M'' [[module isomorphism|isomorphic]] to a direct summand is itself a direct summand. The [[endomorphism ring]] of a continuous module is a [[clean ring]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Continuous modules are clean|last=Camillo|first=V.P.|last2=Khurana|first2=D.|last3=Lam|first3=T.Y.|author3-link=Tsit Yuen Lam|last4=Nicholson|first4=W.K.|last5=Zhou|first5=Y.|journal=Journal of Algebra|doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2006.06.032|volume=304|pages=94–111|year=2006|doi-access=}}</ref>
